title: Per-row changed_at_counter on contacts: correct RFC 8620 §5.6 paging approach
description: Schema V8 adds changed_at_counter to each contacts row. get_changes_since_ordered() returns (peer_user_id, changed_at_counter) tuples; the handler uses the last returned counter as newState on truncation. This is the correct approach for RFC 8620 §5.6: it avoids fetching all rows just to compute a truncated state token, and the ORDER BY changed_at_counter ASC ensures oldest-first paging. A contributor might suggest using the global state counter as newState on truncation (wrong: client would miss items between newState and the last actually-returned counter) or computing per-row state in a separate pass (unnecessary complexity).
